title: 48 Amp EV Charger Wire Size & Breaker for 50 Feet
equipment: Tesla Wall Connector / 48A Level 2 EV Charger
summary: A 48 Amp Level 2 EV charger is classified as a continuous load under NEC rules, requiring a 60A circuit breaker and minimum 6 AWG copper wire for a 50-foot run.
notes: NEC 625.41 requires EV charging circuits to be sized at 125% of the continuous load (48A x 1.25 = 60A).
Standard 6/2 NM-B Romex is rated for 55A at 60°C, so 6 AWG THHN/THWN-2 copper inside 3/4-inch conduit (rated 65A at 75°C) is required for full 48A charging.
Hardwiring is mandatory for 48A chargers since NEMA 14-50 outlets max out at 40A continuous.
wire_item: 6 AWG THHN Copper Wire (50-100 ft Roll)

title: NEMA 14-50 Outlet (40A EV Charger) Wire Size for 75 Feet
equipment: 50A NEMA 14-50 Receptacle for 40A Portable EV Charger
summary: Installing a NEMA 14-50 receptacle 75 feet from the main panel requires 6/3 copper wire (with neutral) and a 50A 2-pole breaker to safely deliver 40A continuous charging.
notes: NEMA 14-50 outlets require 4 wires: two hots, one neutral, and one ground (6/3 cable).
Under NEC 2020/2023, garage EV receptacles require a 50A 2-pole GFCI breaker.
Always buy an industrial-grade EV-rated NEMA 14-50 receptacle to prevent melting under sustained loads.
wire_item: 6/3 NM-B Copper Wire with Ground (75-100 ft)
breaker_item: Industrial Grade NEMA 14-50 EV Outlet + 50A Breaker

title: 32 Amp EV Charger Wire Size & Breaker for 40 Feet
summary: A 32 Amp EV charger requires a 40A circuit breaker (125% continuous load factor) and 8 AWG copper wiring for runs up to 40 feet with minimal voltage drop.
notes: 32A x 1.25 continuous load rule equals 40A minimum circuit rating.
8 AWG copper supports up to 40A in NM-B cable and 50A in THHN conduit.
At 40 feet, voltage drop on 8 AWG copper is just 0.7%, well below the 3% NEC limit.

title: 48 Amp EV Charger Wire Size for 100 Feet Long Run
equipment: 48A Hardwired Wall Charger (Long Detached Garage Run)
summary: For a 100-foot run to a detached garage, upsizing from 6 AWG to 4 AWG copper keeps voltage drop under 1.7% at 48 Amps, ensuring maximum charging speed and zero overheating.
notes: At 100 feet, 6 AWG copper approaches 2.6% voltage drop; stepping up to 4 AWG cuts energy loss by 37%.
Use 1-inch PVC or EMT conduit when pulling three 4 AWG THHN conductors.
Verify your EV charger terminal lugs accept 4 AWG wire (most Tesla and ChargePoint units accept up to 4 AWG).

title: 2000W 12V Inverter Cable Size & Fuse (10 Feet Run)
equipment: 2000W 12V DC Pure Sine Wave Power Inverter
rec_breaker: 250 Amp ANL Fuse or Class T Fuse
summary: A 2000W inverter on a 12V battery bank draws nearly 195A under full load, requiring heavy-duty 2/0 AWG pure copper battery cables and a 250A Class T or ANL fuse.
notes: Formula: 2000W / 12V / 0.85 inverter efficiency = ~196 Amps maximum DC draw.
Low-voltage 12V systems are extremely sensitive to voltage drop; never use copper-clad aluminum (CCA) cables.
Install the 250A fuse within 7 inches of the positive battery terminal.

breaker_item: 250 Amp Class T Fuse Block & Fuse

notes: 3000W / 24V / 0.85 efficiency = 147 Amps continuous peak draw.
Total cable distance includes both positive and negative battery cable lengths combined.
Use hydraulic lug crimpers and adhesive-lined heat shrink for low-resistance terminations.

title: 400W Solar Panel Wire Gauge for 50 Feet Roof Run
equipment: 400W 12V/24V Solar Panel Array to MPPT Charge Controller
rec_breaker: 25 Amp Inline PV Fuse / DC Breaker
summary: A 400W solar array wired in series (24V-40V Vmp) draws around 10A to 20A, making 10 AWG UV-resistant solar PV wire ideal for a 50-foot roof-to-controller run.
notes: Wiring two 200W panels in series doubles voltage (~36V) and halves current (~11A), keeping voltage drop under 1.5% on 10 AWG wire.
Always use UL 4703 sunlight-resistant PV wire with pre-crimped MC4 connectors for outdoor roof runs.
Add a 2-pole DC disconnect breaker between the solar array and your MPPT controller.

title: 50 Amp RV Hookup Wire Size & Breaker for 100 Feet
summary: To power a 50 Amp RV pedestal 100 feet from your main panel without A/C compressor brownouts, install 4 AWG copper THWN or 2 AWG aluminum direct-burial wire.
notes: While 6 AWG copper is rated for 55A-65A, a 100-foot run causes nearly 2.7% voltage drop when dual RV air conditioners start.
Upsizing to 4 AWG copper or 2 AWG aluminum XHHW/URD keeps voltage drop below 1.7% and saves money on long trench runs.
50A RV pedestals require 4 conductors (Hot 1, Hot 2, Neutral, Ground).

title: 30 Amp RV Outlet (TT-30R) Wire Size for 75 Feet
rec_awg_cu: 8 AWG Copper (Upsized from 10 AWG for 120V Drop)
summary: Because 30A RV outlets run on 120V, a 75-foot run experiences double the percentage voltage drop of 240V circuits—requiring 8 AWG copper instead of standard 10 AWG.
notes: CRITICAL: A 30A TT-30R RV outlet is 120V ONLY. Never wire it to a 240V 2-pole breaker or you will destroy all RV electronics.
On 10 AWG wire at 75 feet, 30A at 120V causes a 3.9% voltage drop (exceeding NEC's 3% limit).
Stepping up to 8 AWG copper drops voltage loss to 2.4%, protecting your RV rooftop A/C compressor.

title: 100 Amp Subpanel Wire Size & Breaker for 100 Feet
rec_awg_cu: 3 AWG Copper or 1 AWG Aluminum SER/XHHW
summary: Feeding a 100 Amp subpanel 100 feet away requires 3 AWG copper or 1 AWG aluminum 4-wire feeder cable (2-2-2-4 Al is only rated for 90A) with an isolated neutral bar.
notes: Common mistake: 2-2-2-4 Aluminum SER is rated for 90A max, NOT 100A. Use 1 AWG aluminum or 3 AWG copper for true 100A capacity.
Keep neutral and ground bars strictly separated inside the subpanel and install ground rods if feeding a detached structure.
Voltage drop at 80A realistic load over 100 ft is only 1.7% on 3 AWG copper.

title: 60 Amp Subpanel Wire Size for 60 Feet (Shed / Garage)
rec_awg_cu: 6 AWG Copper (6/3 NM-B) or 4 AWG Aluminum
summary: A 60 Amp subpanel located 60 feet from the main service panel requires 6 AWG copper (rated 65A in THHN, or 55A NM-B rounded up to 60A breaker) or 4 AWG aluminum SER.
notes: Under NEC 240.4(B), 6/3 NM-B copper (55A rating) can be protected by a 60A breaker if the calculated load does not exceed 55A.
For a full 60A continuous rating, pull 6 AWG THHN copper in conduit or use 4-4-4-6 Aluminum SER.
Requires 4 conductors: two hots, one neutral, and one equipment ground.

title: 50 Amp Hot Tub Wire Size & GFCI Breaker (50 Feet)

summary: Outdoor hot tubs require 6 AWG copper THHN conductors inside weatherproof conduit, routed through a 50A GFCI disconnect box mounted at least 5 feet from the water.
notes: NEC 680.42 prohibits standard indoor NM-B Romex outdoors or in wet locations—use THWN-2 copper wire in PVC or Liquidtight conduit.
The GFCI disconnect must be within sight of the hot tub and at least 5 feet away from the inside wall of the spa.
Includes insulated green 10 AWG copper ground wire per NEC Article 680.

title: 50 Amp Welder Outlet (NEMA 6-50R) Wire Size for 30 Feet
summary: Because welders operate on intermittent duty cycles (NEC Article 630), a 50A NEMA 6-50 welder outlet at 30 feet can use 8 AWG THHN copper in conduit or 6/2 NM-B cable.
notes: NEMA 6-50 welder receptacles only require 3 wires: Hot 1, Hot 2, and Ground (no neutral wire needed).
Under NEC 630.11, welder conductors can be sized smaller based on duty cycle, though 6/2 NM-B or 8 AWG THHN gives full 50A headroom.
At 30 feet, voltage drop is negligible (~0.8%), ensuring clean arc starts.

title: 18,000 - 24,000 BTU Mini Split Wire Size & Disconnect (40 ft)
equipment: 240V Ductless Mini Split Heat Pump / Garage A/C
summary: Most 18k to 24k BTU 240V mini-split heat pumps have a Minimum Circuit Ampacity (MCA) under 20A, requiring 12/2 copper wire and a non-fused outdoor AC disconnect box.
notes: Always check the outdoor condenser nameplate for MCA (Minimum Circuit Ampacity) to size wire and MOP (Max Overcurrent Protection) to size the breaker.
HVAC compressor circuits are an exception under NEC Article 440 allowing a 25A or 30A breaker on 12 AWG wire when specified by MOP.
Use a 6-foot 1/2-inch AC whip from the outdoor disconnect box to the condenser.
breaker_item: 60A Non-Fused Outdoor AC Disconnect + 1/2 Inch Whip Kit

title: 7500W 240V Electric Garage Heater Wire Size (45 Feet)
summary: A 7,500W 240V garage heater draws 31.25A continuous, requiring a 40A 2-pole breaker (125% NEC heating rule) and 8/2 copper wire over a 45-foot run.
notes: 7,500W / 240V = 31.25 Amps. Multiplied by 1.25 continuous heating factor = 39.1A -> requires a 40A breaker.
10 AWG wire is rated max 30A and is a fire hazard for 7500W heaters—always use 8 AWG copper.
Hardwired 240V shop heaters only require 2 hot conductors and 1 ground (8/2 cable).
